newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong fighting for independence? Forget it.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong fighting for independence? Forget it.

text.p: If Beijing is even remotely worried that Hong Kong will make a dash for independence or try to topple the Chinese Communist Party, well, FEAR NOT!
A lone protester turned up in front of the Legislative Council building on Friday to demand independence for Hong Kong, which China is taking back from Britain on July 1.

"Macau, Taiwan and places like Tibet and Xinjiang in mainland China should also be independent," said Mok Hon-ying, who said he belongs to an underground group called the Federalist Alliance of China.
Mok had sent a statement out earlier on Friday inviting media to cover the demonstration. But he was the only protester.

Beijing has long warned it would not tolerate any advocacy of independence for Hong Kong, Chinese Nationalist-ruled Taiwan or Tibet. Hong Kong's future leader Tung Chee-hwa has said that protests in the territory that threaten China's "national security" would be suppressed.
But this tough stance has not stopped Mok, a resident of Portugese-ruled Macau, which itself reverts to China in 1999.
"We want to topple the Chinese Communist Party and we want independence for Hong Kong and all the provinces on the mainland," Mok told reporters.

The gaunt-looking Mok, 38, said his party's officers were too afraid to appear in public. He said his alliance, formed four years ago, had about 200 members, many in mainland China and a few in Hong Kong, Macau and Taiwan.
Mok handed in his group's proposal to the secretariat of the Hong Kong legislature, a body which itself will be disbanded upon the handover and replaced by an interim parliament appointed by China.
